_sources: provisions: DED-HOUSE-LOAN provision1961 (s.80EEA) and provision2025 (s.131). summary: S2 s.131(1)–(3); 1961 s.80EEA as inserted by F(No.2)A 2019 s.25, its window extended by FA 2020 s.32 and FA 2021 s.27 (sources M3, M5, M7; D-139, D-147). routes[0]: DED-HOUSE-LOAN. disqualifiers[0]: the row's regimes. disqualifiers[1]: s.131(1) "not eligible to claim deduction under section 130" — ChapterEightNode tries DED-HOUSE-LOAN-EARLIER first. disqualifiers[2]: s.131(2), the row's definition. disqualifiers[3]: s.131(3); W-078.
summary: If you cannot claim the earlier first-house deduction, interest payable on a loan from a financial institution to buy a residential house is deducted up to a limit, where the loan was sanctioned within the later window the Act sets, the house's stamp duty value is within its limit, and you owned no residential house on the date of sanction. The same interest may not be deducted anywhere else. Only the old regime allows it.

routes.name: A loan sanctioned in the later window
routes.description: The interest payable in the year, up to the limit.

disqualifiers.description: It is not deducted in the default regime.
Where the earlier first-house deduction can be claimed, this one cannot.
A loan sanctioned outside the window, a stamp duty value over the limit, or a house already owned on the date of sanction.
The same interest claimed under any other provision, such as house property, is not checked yet.
